questions.prompt: What is the most important lab safety habit?
questions.answer: Think carefully before you act
wrong: Work as fast as you can
Work alone so no one bothers you
questions.explain: Being careful and thoughtful prevents most lab accidents.

questions.prompt: What should you wear to protect your eyes during a lab?
questions.answer: Safety goggles
questions.explain: Goggles protect your eyes from splashes, spills and flying bits.

questions.prompt: Why shouldn't you eat or drink in a science lab?
questions.answer: Food could get mixed with harmful chemicals
wrong: Food makes the lab too warm
Drinks make graphs harder to read
questions.explain: Lab chemicals can be poisonous, so keep food and drinks out of the lab.

questions.prompt: Why should you wear closed-toe shoes in a lab?
questions.answer: To protect your feet from spills and drops
wrong: To help you run faster in the lab
To keep the lab floor clean
questions.explain: If something falls or spills, closed shoes keep it off your skin.

questions.prompt: Why should you tie back long hair in a lab?
questions.answer: It could get caught or catch on fire
wrong: It makes the lab look neater
Long hair blocks the microscope light
questions.explain: Loose hair can tangle in equipment or touch a flame.

questions.prompt: Which piece of lab glassware looks like a cup with a pouring spout?
questions.answer: A beaker
questions.explain: A beaker is a wide glass container with a spout. Its markings give only rough measurements.

questions.prompt: What holds a specimen when you look at it under a microscope?
questions.answer: A slide
questions.explain: A slide is a thin, flat piece of glass that holds what you want to look at.

questions.prompt: What is the safe way to smell a chemical?
questions.answer: Wave the air toward your nose with your hand
wrong: Put your nose right over it
Pour a little on your hand and sniff
questions.explain: This is called wafting. It lets you smell just a little without breathing in a strong dose.

questions.prompt: A chemical splashes into your eye. What should you do?
questions.answer: Rinse it at the eyewash for about 15 minutes
wrong: Wait to see if it starts to hurt
questions.explain: Flushing with lots of water right away washes the chemical out. Tell an adult too.

questions.prompt: How should you treat a small burn from a hot beaker?
questions.answer: Hold it under cold running water
wrong: Rub it with a dry towel
questions.explain: Cool running water for several minutes helps a minor burn. Always tell your teacher.

questions.prompt: What is used to smother a small fire on a person's clothes?
questions.answer: A fire blanket
questions.explain: A fire blanket cuts off air to the flames. The person should also stop, drop and roll.

questions.prompt: Which glassware is like a beaker but has a narrow mouth that can be closed with a stopper?
questions.answer: A flask
questions.explain: A flask's narrow neck makes it easy to close and harder to spill.

questions.prompt: Which lab tool heats things with an open gas flame?
questions.answer: A Bunsen burner
questions.explain: A Bunsen burner makes a flame from gas. A hot plate heats without a flame.

questions.prompt: What is a key rule for using a heat source in the lab?
questions.answer: Never leave it unattended
wrong: Grab hot glass with bare hands
Keep loose paper next to it
questions.explain: Someone should always watch a heat source so a fire or spill can be stopped quickly.

questions.prompt: Mold, blood and dead animals belong in which kind of lab waste?
questions.answer: Biological waste
questions.explain: Biological waste is anything living or once living, which can spread germs.

questions.prompt: Why should you never heat a tightly closed container?
questions.answer: Pressure can build up until it bursts
wrong: The glass will turn into liquid
questions.explain: Heated gases expand. In a sealed container they have nowhere to go, so the container can explode.

questions.prompt: Why shouldn't you throw water on an electrical fire?
questions.answer: Water conducts electricity and can cause shocks
wrong: Water turns the fire into ice
questions.explain: Water won't safely put out an electrical fire. Use the right fire extinguisher and get an adult.

questions.prompt: You find a bottle of clear liquid with no label. What should you do?
questions.answer: Don't use it and tell the teacher
wrong: Smell it to figure out what it is
questions.explain: Clear liquids can be dangerous chemicals. Never use anything from an unlabeled container.

questions.prompt: Leftover rubbing alcohol from an experiment goes in which kind of waste?
questions.answer: Flammable waste
questions.explain: Alcohol catches fire easily, so it is flammable waste.

questions.prompt: Strong acids and old batteries belong in which kind of waste?
questions.answer: Corrosive waste
questions.explain: Corrosive chemicals can eat away at skin and materials, so they need their own container.

questions.prompt: A beaker breaks on the floor. What should you do first?
questions.answer: Keep people away and get an adult
wrong: Pick it up with your bare hands
Kick the pieces under a table
Toss it in the regular trash
questions.explain: Broken glass needs special cleanup and its own sharps or glass waste container.

questions.prompt: You wore gloves while handling a frog in class. Should you still wash your hands?
questions.answer: Yes, always wash your hands afterward
wrong: Only if your hands look dirty
Only if the frog was alive
questions.explain: Germs can still reach your hands, so wash after handling living or once-living things.
